research_question: Among women undergoing hysterectomy for benign gynaecological disease, what is the effect of laparoscopic hysterectomy—laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy (LAVH), total laparoscopic hysterectomy (TLH), or laparoscopic hysterectomy of unspecified type—compared with vaginal hysterectomy on the number of women receiving any blood transfusion intra-operatively, post-operatively during the hospital stay, or through the reported end of follow-up?
treatment_label: Laparoscopic hysterectomy (LAVH, TLH, or laparoscopic hysterectomy of unspecified type)
outcome_description: Binary outcome: number of women who received any blood transfusion (intra-operative or post-operative) out of the number randomised to each arm, assessed during the operation and hospital stay or through the end of reported follow-up. Use intention-to-treat denominators. Do not substitute blood loss volume, haemoglobin drop, or haematoma. Retain double-zero trials visibly, although they contribute no weight to the odds-ratio estimate. Assign treatment and control from procedure descriptions rather than column position. For eligible multi-arm trials with multiple laparoscopic approaches sharing one vaginal-hysterectomy arm, treat each laparoscopic approach as a separate comparison and divide the shared vaginal arm's events and total equally across comparisons; exclude abdominal and robotic arms.
positive_direction: An OR greater than 1 (equivalently, a positive log OR) means that blood transfusion is more frequent with laparoscopic hysterectomy than with vaginal hysterectomy and therefore favors vaginal hysterectomy; an OR less than 1 favors laparoscopic hysterectomy.
search_queries: laparoscopic hysterectomy vaginal hysterectomy randomized trial transfusion
LAVH vaginal hysterectomy controlled trial blood transfusion
total laparoscopic hysterectomy vaginal hysterectomy randomised comparison transfusion
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials directly comparing an eligible laparoscopic hysterectomy approach (LAVH, TLH, or unspecified laparoscopic hysterectomy) with vaginal hysterectomy in women undergoing hysterectomy for benign gynaecological disease.
Trials reporting, or permitting derivation of, the number of women receiving any intra-operative or post-operative blood transfusion and the number randomised in each eligible arm.
Any publication status, language, setting, or follow-up duration, provided the eligible randomised comparison and quantitative transfusion outcome can be identified.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original randomised empirical study, including non-randomised studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers.

No direct comparison between an eligible laparoscopic hysterectomy treatment arm and a vaginal hysterectomy control arm; abdominal and robotic hysterectomy arms are excluded from otherwise eligible multi-arm trials.

No quantitative transfusion outcome data capable of producing an effect size—specifically, no transfusion event counts and arm totals, proportions with recoverable denominators, odds ratio, or other sufficient statistics; blood loss volume, haemoglobin drop, and haematoma alone are insufficient.
Completely unrelated to the research topic or conducted for malignant disease rather than benign gynaecological disease.
moderators_to_extract: Laparoscopic approach subtype (LAVH, TLH, or unspecified)
Timing window for transfusion ascertainment (intra-operative, hospital stay, or longer follow-up)
Trial publication year or surgical era
Risk-of-bias features, including allocation concealment and completeness of intention-to-treat reporting
effect_size_note: Calculate study-specific odds ratios from transfusion event counts with laparoscopic hysterectomy as treatment and vaginal hysterectomy as control, so OR > 1 indicates more transfusions with laparoscopic hysterectomy. Pool using a fixed-effect Mantel-Haenszel model when available; otherwise use a random-effects model. Preserve double-zero studies in the evidence table but give them no weight in the OR synthesis. Use numbers randomised as denominators. For shared-control multi-arm trials, split the vaginal-hysterectomy group's total and events equally across eligible laparoscopic comparisons to avoid double counting; document any fractional allocation and perform an appropriate integer-preserving split if required by software. Pool no outcomes other than receipt of transfusion: specifically exclude operating time, hospital stay, other complications, return to normal activities, conversion to laparotomy, pain, cost, blood loss, haemoglobin change, and haematoma. Follow PRISMA 2020 with duplicate screening, a study flow diagram, duplicate data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment, heterogeneity reporting, sensitivity analyses where feasible, and assessment of reporting bias if enough studies are available.
